title: Scaling Exponent (k-1)/k
content: The growth exponent $\alpha_k = (k-1)/k$ determines how the k-way birthday threshold scales with the number of days $d$: the threshold grows as $d^{\alpha_k}$. For $k=2$: $\alpha = 1/2$ (square root), $k=3$: $\alpha = 2/3$, approaching 1 as $k \to \infty$.

title: Threshold Power Formula
content: Working with the k-th power $n_k^k = k! \cdot d^{k-1}$ avoids fractional exponents. This formulation makes monotonicity and comparison proofs algebraically clean. The factorial factor $k!$ captures the combinatorial growth of coincidence patterns.

title: Exponent Approaches 1
content: As $k \to \infty$, the scaling exponent $(k-1)/k \to 1$, meaning the threshold approaches linear growth in $d$ (the pigeonhole bound). The proof gives an explicit convergence rate: for $(k-1)/k > 1 - \varepsilon$, it suffices to take $k > 1/\varepsilon$.
